To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a novel functional 86-kD glycoproteic antigen, restricted to long-term proliferating human T-cell clones, has been characterized and that this structure is a new member of the Ig superfamily.
we have identified a new 85-kD cell surface antigen expressed on long-term dividing T cells and that this structure plays a regulatory role in T-cell proliferation.
we have isolated an mAb termed anti-AY19 that defines a novel T-cell antigen expressed on long-term dividing human T-lymphocytic lines.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of new cell surface markers on activated T-lymphoid cells.
the identification and characterization of a novel functional T-cell surface structure that may play a role in T-lymphopoiesis.
the isolation and functional characterization of a novel T-cell antigen, the 85-kD AY19 molecule, which may play a role in lymphocyte activation and growth.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the AY 19 mAb defines an 85-kd glycoprotein that is expressed on long-term dividing T lymphocytes and is involved in the negative regulation of T-cell growth.
AY19 defines a new functional structure, the expression of which is restricted to long-term proliferating T-lymphoid cells.
AY19 mAbs recognize a new T-cell activation-associated surface molecule which might be implicated in the regulation of the T-lymphocytic growth.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified a novel functional 80-85-kD glyco-protein on the cell surface which may be involved in the growth control of activated human lymphocytes.

the AY-19 mAb recognizes a new functional T-lymphocytic antigen, which is expressed mainly on long term dividing T-lympho-cytes, and whose ligand could play an important role in the regulation T-lymphocy-tes growth induced by CD 3-TcR stimula-tion.
we have defined a new surface antigen, which is expressed on T-cell clones and T-ALL, and which is involved in the control of the T-cell growth induced by CD2/CD3 interaction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the AY 19 mAb is a novel functional molecule that is expressed on T cells that are in a proliferative state.
the AY-19 mAb defines an 85-kDa cell surface glycoprotein that is restricted to long-term lymphocytic cell lines and T-ALL cells, and that its triggering inhibits CD3-Tc-activated lymphocytes.
we have identified a new functional 85-kDa glycoprotein that is expressed on long term proliferating lymphocytes and whose expression can be modulated by lymphocyte activation.
